args.body:
PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
PREPARED IN ANTICIPATION OF LITIGATION / NEGOTIATION

TO: Engagement Partners
FROM: Negotiation Analysis Team
RE: DPA Counter-Markup Analysis — Deferred Prosecution Agreement for Financial Services Company
DATE: [Date]

====================================================================
I.    EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
====================================================================

We have compared the government's counter-markup of the Deferred Prosecution Agreement ("DPA") against (i) the original DPA as executed/negotiated in the base materials and (ii) our firm's initial markup and negotiating objectives. The government's revision accepts most firm-standard provisions but introduces three material deviations that must be addressed:

    1.  Indemnification — the government silently reduces the indemnification cap and converts the basket from a deductible to a tipping basket;
    2.  Material Adverse Effect ("MAE") Definition — the government adds carve-outs for regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue in this matter; and
    3.  Survival / Limitation Period — the government shortens the survival period for the core representations.

Our negotiating posture, per the controlling partner instruction, is that the client will CONCEDE the basket conversion (deductible-to-tipping) but treats ANY reduction in the survival period for the core representations as a WALK-AWAY issue. The MAE carve-outs and the indemnification cap reduction must therefore be pressed back against the government as central to protecting the client's retained liabilities and exposure to the two pending regulatory inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7.

====================================================================
II.   SCOPE, MATERIALS REVIEWED, AND METHODOLOGY
====================================================================

In preparing this memorandum we identified and reviewed in full every document in the matter folder relevant to this engagement:

    • Base / Original DPA (Matter File 26 — White Collar Defense Investigations): the operative DPA negotiated between the parties, containing representations and warranties, covenants, conditions to closing, indemnification, and termination provisions applicable to the financial services client.
    • Government's Counter-Markup: the counterparty revision accepted in most respects but introducing the three deviations analyzed below.
    • Schedules and Exhibits: disclosure schedules qualifying the base materials, including Schedule 3.7 (pending regulatory inquiries), Schedule 5.2 (retained liabilities), and Exhibit B (survival matrix), which control over general statements in the base DPA.
    • Deal Team Correspondence: partner email thread; the LATEST message controls and revises earlier priority ordering. Under the controlling instruction, the client concedes the basket conversion but treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue.

We also verified that certain other documents on the shared matter index (administrative correspondence files and unrelated CUAD/deep-drafting packs) concern different engagements and were excluded from this analysis.

Methodology: For each of the government's deviations, we (1) identify the base provision and our initial markup position, (2) describe the government's change, (3) reconcile the change against the controlling schedules/exhibits and partner instructions, and (4) recommend an accept/reject/counter position together with any concession or walk-away implications.

====================================================================
III.  DEVIATION 1 — INDEMNIFICATION: CAP REDUCTION AND BASKET CONVERSION (DEDUCTIBLE → TIPPING)
====================================================================

Base Provision and Our Initial Position:
The original DPA contains an indemnification regime under which the client bears exposure up to a defined cap, subject to a deductible-style basket. Under our initial markup, the cap and the deductible structure were firm-standard: the client is indemnified for losses only once the aggregate threshold is crossed and only above that threshold (deductible mechanics), protecting the client from first-dollar exposure.

Government's Counter-Markup Change:
The government's revision (i) silently reduces the indemnification cap and (ii) converts the basket from a deductible to a tipping basket. A tipping basket treats the full amount of losses (including amounts below the threshold) as recoverable once the basket is tripped, materially expanding the client's monetary exposure as compared to a deductible structure. Coupled with the cap reduction, the government's change both lowers the ceiling of protection and expands the floor/aggregation mechanics, a compounded adverse shift.

Reconciliation Against Schedules:
Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that the markup's indemnification changes would silently shift. The government's cap reduction and tipping-basket mechanics would re-allocate a meaningful portion of these retained liabilities onto the client by compressing the band of the government's indemnity obligation and expanding the client's aggregable loss pool. Because scheduled exceptions control over general statements, any concession on the indemnification structure must be measured against the Schedule 5.2 liabilities to avoid silent assumption of unexpected exposure.

Controlling Partner Instruction:
The client will CONCEDE the basket conversion — that is, we will accept the deductibles-to-tipping conversion. This is an express, authorized concession.

Recommendation on the Indemnification Deviation:
• ACCEPT the basket conversion (deductible → tipping basket), consistent with the controlling partner instruction and as a negotiating chip.
• REJECT (counter) the silent reduction in the indemnification cap. The cap reduction is not within the conceded scope and, when combined with the tipping-basket expansion, would severely erode protection for the Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities. We should preserve the original cap, or at minimum seek a cap level that, together with the tipping structure, maintains the client's total exposure within the original negotiated envelope.
• Tie any concession on the cap to a commensurate government concession elsewhere (e.g., deletion or narrowing of the MAE carve-outs, discussed below).

====================================================================
IV.   DEVIATION 2 — MATERIAL ADVERSE EFFECT CARVE-OUTS FOR REGULATORY ACTION
====================================================================

Base Provision and Our Initial Position:
The DPA's MAE definition, as negotiated, captures the ordinary circumstances in which the client's affairs materially deteriorate such that the government can invoke protections. Our initial markup did not include carve-outs, or included narrower carve-outs, leaving the definition balanced and free of self-serving exclusions that would gut the MAE concept of meaning.

Government's Counter-Markup Change:
The government adds carve-outs to the MAE definition for regulatory action "of exactly the kind at issue in this matter." This is a targeted, matter-specific carve-out designed to exclude the very regulatory exposure that is the subject of the DPA from being treated as an MAE, thereby insulating the government from the consequences of those regulatory developments and shifting the risk to the client.

Reconciliation Against Schedules:
Schedule 3.7 discloses TWO pending regulatory inquiries that intersect the markup's MAE carve-outs. The government's carve-outs are directly calibrated to these two inquiries. If accepted, the carve-outs would strip MAE protection precisely where the client's risk is concentrated — the two pending regulatory inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7 — and would effectively relieve the government of the burden of those developments while inviting the client to absorb them. This is flatly inconsistent with the original allocation of regulatory risk and is the most consequential deviation in the markup.

Controlling Partner Instruction:
The instruction does not authorize any concession on the MAE carve-outs. It only concedes the basket conversion; all else remains subject to negotiation, and the survival issue is a walk-away.

Recommendation on the MAE Deviation:
• REJECT (counter) the MAE carve-outs in full. The carve-outs are matter-specific exclusions directed at the two pending regulatory inquiries on Schedule 3.7, and accepting them would eviscerate the client's protection in the exact area of exposure the parties knowingly negotiated. 
• At a minimum, if the government insists on some carve-out language, counter-propose language that is general and non-targeted, does not reference "regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue," and preserves the client's rights with respect to the two disclosed pending inquiries.
• Leverage the basket-conversion concession to extract deletion or substantial narrowing of these carve-outs; the concession on basket mechanics should have purchase here because it is a real, quantifiable concession by the client.

====================================================================
V.    DEVIATION 3 — SURVIVAL / LIMITATION PERIOD SHORTENED FOR CORE REPRESENTATIONS — WALK-AWAY ISSUE
====================================================================

Base Provision and Our Initial Position:
Exhibit B sets the survival matrix for the DPA's representations. Under the original DPA, the core representations survive for the lengths specified in Exhibit B, which reflect the parties' negotiated allocation of post-execution risk over time.

Government's Counter-Markup Change:
The government introduces a new limitation period that shortens the survival period for the core representations, directly contradicting the survival matrix in Exhibit B. This is a unilateral narrowing of the window during which a breach of the core representations can be enforced, materially reducing the client's (and the parties') ability to pursue claims.

Reconciliation Against Schedules:
Exhibit B sets the survival matrix the markup's limitation-period change contradicts. Because schedules and exhibits control over general statements in the base materials, Exhibit B governs the survival periods; the government's new limitation period would override, in its favor, the agreed schedule.

Controlling Partner Instruction:
This is the controlling red line: the client treats any survival-period reduction for the core representations as a WALK-AWAY issue. The deal correspondence expressly identified this as non-negotiable — no reduction in the survival period for the core representations will be accepted.

Recommendation on the Survival / Limitation Deviation:
• REJECT outright — WALK-AWAY. Do not accept any shortening of the survival period for the core representations, regardless of any concession offered by the government in exchange. The survival matrix in Exhibit B must be preserved in full.
• This position is fixed by the controlling partner instruction and is not available for trade. We should communicate to the government that any requirement of shortened survival is a deal-breaker.

====================================================================
VI.   NEGOTIATION STRATEGY AND PRIORITY MATRIX
====================================================================

Based on the above, we recommend the following consolidated negotiation posture:

  Deviation                                   Position            Tradeable?
  ------------------------------------------  ------------------  -------------
  1a. Indemnification cap reduction           COUNTER (reject)    Tradeable, but requires offset
  1b. Basket conversion (deductible→tipping)  ACCEPT (concede)    Conceded per partner instruction
  2.  MAE carve-outs for regulatory action    REJECT (counter)    Tradeable for carve-out narrowing
  3.  Survival / limitation-period reduction  REJECT — WALK-AWAY  NOT tradeable

Key Strategy Points:
1. Concede the basket conversion immediately and openly; it positions the client as reasonable and buys goodwill for the harder fights.
2. Hold firm against the MAE carve-outs; deploy the Schedule 3.7 pending-inquiry analysis as the factual basis for why the carve-outs are targeted and unacceptable.
3. Insist on preserving the indemnification cap consistent with the Schedule 5.2 retained-liability exposure; reject the silent cap reduction.
4. Draw a hard, non-negotiable line on the survival-period reduction per Exhibit B and the partner instruction. Any survival reduction is a walk-away.

We should also flag for the client that the combination of the cap reduction and the tipping basket, if both were accepted, would materially expand net exposure relative to the original DPA; therefore the two indemnification elements must be negotiated together so that a concession on the basket is not accompanied by a stealth cap reduction.

====================================================================
VII.  CONCLUSION
====================================================================

The government's counter-markup is largely consistent with the base DPA but introduces three material deviations: (1) a silent reduction of the indemnification cap plus a deductible-to-tipping basket conversion; (2) targeted MAE carve-outs for the exact regulatory inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7; and (3) a shortened survival/limitation period for the core representations that contradicts Exhibit B.

We are authorized to concede the basket conversion.
